question_papers.paper_title: Set 1 - Chapter 3 Practice Paper (Angles as Turns)

questions.question_text: An angle measuring exactly 90 degrees is called a:
What type of angle is 50 degrees?
Degree measure of one full turn is:
At 1:00, what angle do clock hands form?
Facing North, turn 90° clockwise. Which direction do you face?
How many right angle turns make a 1/2 turn (180°) and a full turn (360°)?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1/2 turn = 2 right angles. Full turn = 4 right angles.

questions.question_text: A minute hand moves from 12 to 3. Calculate the fraction of turn and degree measure.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Fraction = 15/60 = 1/4. Angle = 90°.

questions.question_text: Facing East, turn 180° clockwise, then 90° anti-clockwise. Final facing direction?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Facing West after 180°, then North after 90° anti-clockwise.

sections.section_name: Section C (Long Answer & Case Study Questions)

questions.question_text: Classify the following angle measures: 30°, 90°, 110°, 180°. Draw clock positions for 3:00 and 6:00.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Acute, Right, Obtuse, Straight. 3:00 = 90°, 6:00 = 180°.

questions.question_text: Case Study: A crane boom rotates 30° clockwise from East. (a) Is the angle acute or obtuse? (b) How many degrees more needed to complete a right angle or straight angle?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Classification based on degree. Remaining degrees calculated by subtracting from 90° or 180°.
